newsitem.title: INDIA: Poland sees inflation fall to 13 pct by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Poland sees inflation fall to 13 pct by year-end.

text.p: Poland's inflation rate is expected to fall to 13 percent by the year-end from 17 percent at the end of 1996, first Deputy Prime Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Friday.

Kolodko, who is also Poland's Finance Minister, told a business conference in Calcutta that inflation, which was 70 percent in 1990, continued to be a worry amid an all-round improvement in the economy.
"Despite decreasing inflation...(it) is still causing several problems and counteracting it is one of the priorities of our policy," he said.
"The rate of inflation is expected to decline by 1997 year-end to 13 percent and to a single digit within a year and a half or so," he said.

The East European nation, which witnessed difficulties in its transition to a market economy from the Cold War days of socialist planning, has successfully entered the international financial markets, he said.

"The invitation extended last July to join the OECD (Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development) gives us the stamp of approval as an open, advanced market economy, thus concluding a stage in transition," Kolodko said.
"I may say: we have made it."
Gross domestic product (GDP), which fell by 18 percent between 1990 and 1992, increased by around 20 percent between 1994 and 1996, he said.
Aided by exports, the GDP was expected to touch $200 billion by 2000, Kolodko said.
The budget deficit, which was close to 7.0 percent of GDP in 1992, has since 1993 been below 3.0 percent and now stands at 2.7 percent, he said.
